//: §5.3 of the blueprint: 'Compiler options are never redefined per workspace - change the base.'
This config used to extend the Node flavour and then hand-copy `lib` back to
["ES2022", "DOM", "DOM.Iterable"], which is a compiler option redefined per workspace.
The lib flavour already declares exactly that list under the display 'browser + React component
library', so the correct fix was to point at it rather than to restate it: transport's core is a
fetch client and its types are `Response` and `BodyInit`, so it needs the DOM lib, and it never
needed the Node one. The flavour's `jsx: react-jsx` is inert here - this package has no .tsx file,
and jsx only changes how .tsx is parsed.
The core is framework-free, and this package's own typecheck covers only the core.
src/next.ts is excluded on purpose: it is a thin adapter over next/headers, and making the
package depend on a framework to typecheck a few lines of adapter is the wrong direction. Each
consuming app typechecks it as part of itself, which is where the framework actually is.
